chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, from the one who reported it, from Abu Maryam al-Ansari, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
That al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) enshrouded Usamah ibn Zayd in a red cloak of Hibrah, and that Ali (peace be upon him) enshrouded Sahl ibn Hunayf in a red cloak of Hibrah.

key_terms.حِبَرَةٍ: A specific type of fabric or texture, often described as red or mixed-color wool

ai.seo_question: What type of fabric did the Imams use for shrouding the deceased?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the practical application of the 'Hibrah' fabric—a red cloth with small black spots—by the Imams, demonstrating a tradition of modesty and simplicity in burial attire rather than ostentation. It serves as a key textual basis in Shia jurisprudence for the permissibility and recommendation of using patterned or colored fabrics for shrouds, contrasting with later practices that favored plain white linen. The narration underscores the continuity of prophetic customs through the Ahl al-Bayt, linking the burial of Usamah ibn Zayd and Sahl ibn Hunayf to the broader ethical framework of dignified death.

en.hubeali:
Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ayoub Bin Nuh, from the one who reported it, from Abu Maryam Al Ansary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>
that Al-Hassanasws Bin Aliasws enshrouded Asama Bin Zayd with a red cloak of Hibra (a type of fabric), and that Aliasws enshrouded Sahl Bin Huneyf with a red cloak of Hibra’.
en.sarwar: 9. Sahl ibn Ziyad has narrated from Ayyub ibn Nuh from those whom he has mentioned from abu Maryam al-Ansariy who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

has said that abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, shrouded ‘Usamah ibn Zayd with a red Burd which was made in Hibarah and Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, shrouded Sahl ibn Hunayf with a red Burd which was made in Hibarah.”
